findings.current: a great power: the Nangong Family
findings.defect: The Korean describes the Nangong Family as a great tree, preserving a specific image that the accepted baseline also retained. “A great power” conveys prominence but drops that image.
findings.rationale: The source uses 거목, literally “great tree,” as a metaphor for the family’s stature.
findings.replacement: a great tree: the Nangong Family

findings.current: can make the weak feel even more powerless and wretched
findings.defect: The Korean compares the misery caused by comfort with the weak person’s existing helplessness. The current wording instead says comfort intensifies both powerlessness and misery.
findings.rationale: The comparison in the source is 비참함보다 더한—misery greater than helplessness—not greater helplessness and misery.
findings.replacement: can make the weak feel even more wretched than their own helplessness

findings.defect: “I promise” adds an explicit pledge that the Korean does not state.
findings.rationale: The source says “It will be that way. Definitely,” referring to their meeting with genuine smiles; it does not explicitly make a promise.

summary: The translation is largely faithful. I found a small loss of imagery and two minor shifts in meaning.
